speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To better understand your gait and limb ataxia, have you noticed any changes in your balance or coordination over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; does the clumsiness worsen with fatigue or specific movements, and have you experienced any numbness or weakness in your extremities? Additionally, do you have a history of diabetes or alcohol use disorder, which are common precursors to such symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, which carries a risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), I need to see your latest MRI. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI. While we await those, have you recently developed any new visual disturbances, cognitive changes, or weakness on one side of the body?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI. I need to see the scan immediately to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions in the parieto-occipital regions, which is the classic presentation for your condition.
